entities.summary:
The Battle of Dakar was a pivotal event in World War II, as a combined French and British force attempted to hold the strategic port city against a Vichy French naval squadron and a German air force. 

 On September 23, 1940, the British and French ships engaged the German aircraft carrier Graf Zeppelin, but were unable to prevent the German planes from sinking several British ships. 

 The battle was a significant defeat for the Allies, but it also marked the beginning of a new phase in the war, as the German air force began to play a more prominent role in the conflict. 

 The legacy of the Battle of Dakar can be seen in the increased importance of air power in modern warfare, as well as the continued strategic importance of the port city of Dakar.
